A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPL research, and their complete pages, equations, figures and tables support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. V2 refers to an implementation appendix, but its contents are not included in the supplied file.

before.justification: V1 reports original PPL benchmark results, patch-occlusion experiments, robustness tests, training/TDE analyses and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original PPL results on GenImage, DRCT and Chameleon, alongside robustness experiments and component ablations. Retained original results also qualify.

M1.justification: The RPR procedure, patch-wise contrastive loss and weighted cross-entropy objective remain unchanged in Equations 2–4, using CLIP/DINOv2 with LoRA. Renaming the contrastive margin from m to alpha and expanding its explanation do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: GenImage, DRCT, Chameleon and the image-detection task remain. V2 Figure 6(a) adds evaluated resizing conditions, extending input-corruption coverage. Although v1 Figure 9's caption mentions resizing, its actual plots show only JPEG compression and Gaussian blur.

E2.justification: V2 adds Effort to the GenImage comparison in Table 1 and DRCT to the JPEG/blur robustness comparisons. LNP disappears from the Chameleon comparison. GramNet is omitted from the detailed Chameleon table but remains in the overview Figure 1.

E3.justification: V2 Table 3 adds SDv1.4-only training for Chameleon evaluation and separate fake/real accuracies. Random-masking evaluation is stated to cover all GenImage, versus SDv1.4 in v1 Figure 10's caption. V2 also corrects the stated blur sigmas to 0.5–2.5, matching v1's plotted axis; this does not establish rerunning that experiment.

E4.justification: The supplied v2 omits v1 Figure 7 and its training-loss and normalized-TDE distribution analyses, plus all three hyperparameter sweeps in v1 Table 4. Component ablations and patch-masking analyses remain, while resizing robustness is added. This substantially changes the evidence examining PPL's mechanism and sensitivity.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3's high-impact, low-impact and random-patch curves become a median-impact curve with a shaded impact range in v2 Figure 3(b). This changes the statistical summary, although the range's construction is unspecified. Neither version provides repeated-run or seed information; the across-generator standard deviations and 18.7% ± 4.1% statement remain.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands Chameleon results with SDv1.4-only training and class-specific accuracies, adds robustness results, and omits the training/TDE and hyperparameter-sweep results. Under the stated all-GenImage training condition, DINOv2 accuracy changes from 70.51% in v1 Figure 8 to 72.07% in v2 Table 3, although v2 Figure 1 still shows 70.5%. Existing PPL GenImage and DRCT table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Section 4 defines the normalized diagnostic score exp(TDE(i,j) − TDEmax); this definition disappears with its analysis in v2. The four central equations remain mathematically equivalent, including the renamed contrastive margin. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the two patch-utilization principles, Few-Patch Bias attributed to lazy learning, the two-component PPL framework, and claims of improved generalization and robustness across two evaluation settings. The contribution's scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly states that modern text-to-image models exceed existing benchmark image quality, expanding v1's brief future-data discussion. It removes the interpretation of early loss collapse as shortcutting and the explanation that excessive patch replacement creates an overly difficult learning problem. The general lazy-learner explanation remains.

D1.justification: V1 specifies 14×14 patches, RPR probability 0.9, replacement ratio 50%, contrastive weight 0.3 and margin 1.0. V2 omits these defaults and refers to an appendix absent from the supplied PDF. It adds test-time center cropping, zero-filled TDE masking and a 30 GB GPU-memory requirement. The available reproducibility information changes substantially, without establishing changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds TextureCrop and GPT-ImgEval citations and removes Learning on Gradients. Related work adds TextureCrop's sliding-window and texture-selection approach while retaining the local/global positioning. Effort was already cited in v1; its new evaluated comparison is a separate baseline change.

P1.justification: Most abstract, contribution and method prose remains recognizable. V2 makes limited paragraph and caption rewrites, removes the analysis and hyperparameter subsections, introduces a standalone Limitations and Future Work section, revises the conclusion, and updates the author/affiliation block.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two columns to one and extensively reorganizes the visuals: redesigned overview/framework diagrams, merged attention and occlusion panels, a transposed TDE heatmap, a Chameleon table replacing the detailed bar chart, and consolidated robustness plots. The training/TDE figure and hyperparameter table disappear. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The expanded Chameleon reporting and robustness comparisons are useful. However, v2 loses key implementation defaults, sensitivity studies and training/TDE evidence supporting its retained mechanism claims; the promised appendix is absent. Its Chameleon table also conflicts with its overview figure. These losses weaken reproducibility and coherence, outweighing the additions, while the retained method, main benchmark results and component ablation limit the overall decline.
